title: Legacy sampling default propagate causing trailing-prompt-noise in customer evals
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers reported deterministic eval regressions and truncated JSON payloads starting after a runtime merge (config_fallback_v2) that changed how sampling defaults and stop-token normalization are applied. Symptom: customer evals that previously returned exact JSON objects or stopped at explicit end-markers now either include trailing partial tokens, extra punctuation, or omit the terminating marker entirely, causing downstream evals to fail. Affected environments: Hosted API, Dedicated pools with per-customer config overrides, and Private (VPC) deployments using older per-tenant config templates.

Root cause hypothesis: The new config_fallback_v2 path introduced a precedence inversion between sampling defaults and explicit stop token lists for requests where the request payload omits sampling fields (common for eval harnesses that rely on server-side defaults). When a request had no sampling keys, the runtime applied legacy sampling defaults (temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0) AND performed a normalization step that canonicalized stop token strings (removed trailing whitespace and non-UTF8 bytes). For some customers whose stop tokens intentionally included trailing whitespace or invisible separators, normalization removed the effective terminator. Combined with deterministic sampling, the generator produced deterministic but semantically different outputs (either running past the intended stop or emitting partial continuations).

Why this escaped tests: Unit tests validated tokenization and sampling independently, but none covered the cross-product of (a) inheritance of sampling defaults, (b) stop-token normalization edgecases, and (c) per-tenant override behavior across hosted/dedicated/private. Test infra mostly exercised hosted defaults; private deployment templates using older patterns were not included in the canaries for this change.

Immediate impact: Two enterprise customers reported failing nightly evals and blocked CI pipelines. One customer (Acrobatix) observed corrupted CSV/JSON outputs in their retention pipeline, causing webhook retries and downstream SLA violations. We throttled and coordinated immediate mitigations while building a safe runtime fix.

Relevant artifacts and links: PR with the config change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812
Canary dashboard (tokens-overrun metric): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/serving/tokens-overrun?panelId=3
Customer bug report (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Acrobatix+Eval+Regression
Reproducer used in staging: curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<PROMPT>","stop":["END\n"],"max_tokens":64}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

Decision so far: do a scoped hotfix that restores stop-token precedence over sampling-default application and adds a conservative normalization that preserves visible trailing separators. We will also add a runtime feature-flag gate for config_fallback_v2 behavior so we can toggle the new logic per-deployment level while we sweep tests and templates.

Proposed permanent fix: (1) Update the runtime request handling to evaluate stop-token list precedence before any sampling-default substitution. If an explicit stop list is present (even if empty), it must be honored exactly unless the customer opts into normalization. (2) Introduce a per-tenant flag keep_stop_token_exact that defaults to true for Dedicated/Private and false for Hosted (to preserve existing hosted normalizations). (3) Improve tests: add integration test cases for stop tokens containing trailing whitespace, invisible unicode separators, and non-UTF8 byte sequences. Expand end-to-end suites to run against a representative dedicated pool template and a private template.

Rollout plan: 1) Patch release runtime-1.20.3-hotfix with stop-token precedence bugfix; deploy as a canary to one hosted region and one dedicated pool currently used by Acrobatix. 2) Enable feature-flag-based fallback for private deployments and coordinate with Solutions Eng to roll updated templates. 3) Monitor tokens-overrun, eval-failure-rate, and customer-specific regression dashboards for 48 hours. 4) Promote to all regions and dedicated pools after green canary.

Communication: Notified affected customers with interim mitigation (we accepted a manual per-tenant config override that set stop tokens explicitly and disabled normalization). Customer success drafted a technical notification and will schedule follow-ups with Engineering for RCA and timeline.

Postmortem actions: add test coverage (integration + fuzzing of stop tokens); add a lint to deployment templates to detect missing sampling fields; run a one-off scanning job across all private templates to flag those that rely on implicit server-side sampling defaults.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a request that omits sampling fields and supplies an explicit stop token with trailing whitespace (e.g., "END\n").
2) Send to a runtime with config_fallback_v2 enabled (staging environment reproduction available).
3) Observe output continues past the stop marker or returns truncated JSON missing final terminator.
Minimal curl reproducer: curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"{\"input\": \"test\"}","stop":["END\n"],"max_tokens":16}'
acceptance_criteria: Runtime enforces explicit stop-token precedence over sampling default substitution.
Canary shows no increase in tokens-overrun metric for affected customers after patch deployment.
Integration tests covering trailing whitespace and invisible separator stop tokens added and green in CI.
Private/dedicated deployment templates updated or flagged; Solutions Eng notified with rollout timeline.
